column1: # config/macos/defaults.tsv - macOS user defaults install.sh applies.
# Input to the installer, not an installed file: there is no target path to link,
# so this has no manifest.tsv row (the manifest maps a tracked FILE onto a
# target). install.sh reads it in the `macos` group; --skip-macos-defaults opts
# out; bin/dotfiles-doctor --only macos verifies each row against the live value.
# Tab-separated. Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are comments.
# Columns:  scope<TAB>domain<TAB>key<TAB>type<TAB>value<TAB>note
# scope    currentHost  per-machine preference (defaults -currentHost ...).
#                       Required for keys macOS itself only reads per-host;
#                       written to ~/Library/Preferences/ByHost/, so it does not
#                       follow a synced or migrated home directory.
#          any          the ordinary all-hosts domain (defaults ...).
# domain   preference domain. NSGlobalDomain is the global one and is accepted
#          alongside -currentHost.
# type     int | float | bool | string. Becomes the -int/-float/-bool/-string
#          flag on `defaults write`; a bool reads back as 1/0, which the
#          installer accounts for when deciding whether a row already matches.
# value    the value to write.
# note     why this value, and what it costs. Same rule as manifest.tsv: only
#          what cannot be read off the key name.
# Nothing here is identity or machine state - these are preferences, portable to
# any Mac. A key whose right value differs per machine does not belong in a
# tracked file at all.
# ---- menu bar ----
# Both keys are unset by default; macOS then uses 12pt spacing and 16pt selection
# padding. At 2 the bar fits far more items before macOS starts hiding them under
# a notched display's camera housing, which is the whole point.
# These take effect when a status item is CREATED, not when the pref is written:
# every already-running app keeps its old spacing until it is relaunched. The
# installer restarts the two processes that own the system-side items; a
# third-party menubar app needs its own relaunch (setup.md records this).
currentHost
column6: Gap between menu bar status items. Lower is tighter; 0 makes adjacent icons touch with no gap at all.

column6: Padding of the click-highlight drawn around a status item. Keep it at or near the spacing above: a value much larger re-inflates the bar the spacing just tightened, and 0 makes the highlight hug the glyph.
